title: PRD: Bounded Progressive Emit Protocol — schema predicates, retry semantics & streaming error windows
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Problem: Customers running streaming structured responses with function/tool calls see two categories of failures: transient frame truncation (partial JSON fragments) and persistent tool-side errors that break client-side parsers. This PRD defines a bounded progressive emit protocol that pairs schema predicates with explicit checkpoint frames, idempotency tokens for tool invocation, and a streaming error window to control retries and degrade gracefully. Goal: eliminate class-A consumer parsing failures while preserving low-latency streaming for large payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Schema predicate handshake: first frame MUST include 'schema_predicate' metadata matching the model stream. When predicate mismatches, server sends a 'schema_mismatch' control frame and stops progressive emits for that request.

Checkpoint frames: emitter MUST insert a 'checkpoint' frame at most every 4 KB of emitted JSON or every 5 seconds, whichever occurs first. Checkpoints include a monotonic checkpoint_id and a byte-offset anchor for resumability.

Idempotent tool invocation: tool-calls originating from streamed emit must include an idempotency_token derived from request_id + checkpoint_id. Replay within a 5-minute window should be accepted and deduplicated by downstream tool gateways.

Streaming error window: transient frames that fail local parse (incomplete JSON) trigger up to 2 supervised retransmit attempts of the last checkpoint window. Retransmits must be scoped to the bytes between the last checkpoint and current offset and capped at 64 KB total retry bytes.

Graceful tool fallback: if tool invocation returns a non-retriable error code or exceeds 3 retries, runtime switches to a compatible fallback model variant and emits a 'fallback_notice' control frame before continuing streaming.

Partial emit isolation: consumers receiving partial objects must be able to reconcile by applying checkpoint anchors; checkpoints guarantee consistent object boundaries for objects < 2 KB. If an object spans >2 KB, the emitter must emit a 'fragment_marker' with sequence index to enable reassembly.

Observability hooks: every control frame (schema_mismatch, checkpoint, fallback_notice, fragment_marker, retry_attempt) MUST emit a telemetry event with tags: request_id, model, route, checkpoint_id, and error_code where applicable.

Backward compatibility: when clients do not understand control frames, they should be able to ignore unknown frames and still parse core JSON objects; control frames must be emitted as newline-prefixed JSON objects with a reserved header 'rw-control' to avoid confusing naive parsers.

E2E test coverage: automated e2e tests must simulate mid-stream tool failure, partial frame delivery, and checkpoint-based resumptions with assertions on client parse success and at-least-once/at-most-once tool call semantics as specified below.

Performance SLO: enabling bounded progressive emit for 99th percentile streaming latency must not increase token-latency by more than 10% in our standard workload compared to baseline streaming without the protocol enabled.
implementation_notes:
Implementation will add a control-frame layer above existing streaming socket. Control frames are small JSON blobs prefixed with '
' and starting with header 'rw-control'. Runtime must maintain per-request checkpoint state and map idempotency_token -> tool call result for 5 minutes. Kernel scheduling should prevent checkpoint inserts from blocking token emission; implement as asynchronous sidecar streamer.
test_cases: TC-1: schema mismatch: send client predicate mismatch; expect schema_mismatch frame and clean stream termination with telemetry event.
TC-2: checkpoint resumability: stream until checkpoint, simulate connection drop, reconnect using last checkpoint_id and resume from anchor; client reconstructs valid JSON objects.

TC-3: tool transient error: simulate tool returning transient error twice then success; runtime retries using idempotency_token and emits retry_attempt telemetry and final tool result included in stream.

TC-4: tool fatal error: simulate permanent tool error; runtime switches to fallback model variant, emits fallback_notice, and continues streaming; client receives fallback_notice event and subsequent outputs.
TC-5: partial object >2KB: emitter produces fragment_marker sequence; client reassembles fragments in order and validates object integrity via checksum header.
TC-6: unknown-control-client: client that ignores control frames still parses core JSON objects without errors.
TC-7: perf regression: run 99th percentile latency benchmark with protocol ON and OFF and assert <=10% regression.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Tracing: attach checkpoint_id to request span and annotate retried segments
Alert: >0.5% of streams per hour with schema_mismatch -> alert SRE pager
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flag gated rollout to internal customers and staging (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in beta for selected customers with high streaming usage (4 weeks). Phase 3: gradual ramp to 25% production traffic with telemetry validation (2 weeks). Phase 4: full rollout after meeting stability and perf gates. Holdback: ability to disable control-frames and revert to legacy streaming in runtime config.
decisions: Control frame format: newline-prefixed JSON with header 'rw-control' chosen over binary framing to preserve backwards compatibility with simple HTTP stream parsers.
Retry budget: bounded to 64KB per window to avoid unbounded retransmit costs.
Idempotency retention: 5 minutes judged sufficient for typical reconnect patterns; revisit if customers require longer windows.
risks: Clients that rely on strict byte-stream framing may misinterpret control frames despite header; mitigation: document header and provide client SDK update.
Checkpoint insertion may add CPU overhead on very high throughput paths; mitigation: optimize checkpoint generation and offload to sidecar thread.
Tool deduplication state increases memory pressure on gateway; mitigation: LRU eviction and metrics to monitor dedup table size.
